project_specification.addition_summary: Add feature 50 to the Point-in-Time feature-store plugin: the FeatureMaterialiser counts how many requests reuse an already-materialised feature instead of recomputing it, exposing a cache_hit counter so the laziness of feature 49 is measurable. The counter is incremented on the reuse path (a hit that returns the stored Parquet without calling the definition) and reported on the MaterialisedFeature result, so a caller can observe reuse without timing or comparing payloads.

existing_context.test_baseline: feature-store suite under tests/feature-store/, run with pyarrow installed
existing_context.conventions: snake_case modules, frozen dataclasses for value types, docstrings that cite app_spec.xml feature numbers and docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md sections, stdlib-only keying/row layers, third-party imports (pyarrow) deferred to first use, @register only in the package __init__ (never a submodule), degrade-don't-break composition. Tests assert on observed behaviour (call counts) rather than values, with long narrative docstrings explaining the "why".

category.name: Feature Store Caching
category.feature: System exposes a cache_hit counter on the FeatureMaterialiser that is incremented every time a request reuses an already-materialised feature instead of recomputing it, returning a non-negative integer count so the laziness of feature 49 is measurable
System reports the cache_hit count on each MaterialisedFeature result so a caller reads reuse off the return value rather than inferring it from timing
System exposes a cache_hit_rate property (hits over total materialise calls) that returns a ratio in [0, 1], so the reuse depth of the lake is measurable
System resets the cache_hit counters with an explicit reset method that returns both counters to zero, so a replay window or a test can bound the measurement

category.name: Feature Store Caching Verification
category.feature: System passes an end-to-end test in which the first materialise call computes and reports a miss, the second call reuses the stored file without calling the definition, increments cache_hit, and returns the identical rows

project_specification.integration_points: Extends FeatureMaterialiser.materialise (packages/feature-store/src/feature_store/materialise.py) to increment the counter on the reuse path Extends MaterialisedFeature with the observed hit/miss facts Covered by tests/feature-store/test_materialise.py
project_specification.constraints: Must not change feature 49's observable behaviour: a hit still does not call compute, a miss still computes and writes, replace=True still recomputes deliberately, a corrupt lake is still refused not recomputed Must not touch the FeatureKey, FeatureStore, or any shared file (src/app/middleware.py, src/app/settings.py, migrations/**, alembic/**) The counter is a process-memory measurement, never persisted to the lake — a fresh materialiser over the same lake starts at zero, matching feature 49's disk-only persistence Follow the existing docstring discipline: cite app_spec.xml feature 50 and the materialise module's existing cross-references to it All existing feature-store tests must stay green

implementation_steps.phase: Add a cache_hit counter to FeatureMaterialiser, incremented on the reuse path in materialise() Report the hit/miss fact on MaterialisedFeature and expose cache_hit / cache_hit_rate / reset accessors
Add end-to-end tests asserting the counter increments on reuse and not on a miss, and that the reused rows are identical

project_specification.success_criteria: Feature 50 implemented and measured at the materialise seam cache_hit increments exactly once per reuse and never on a compute All existing feature-store tests still green; new caching tests green
